title: Ultra-rare Cristiano Ronaldo card sells for record $1.35 million
content:
A one-of-a-kind Cristiano Ronaldo trading card sold for $1.35 million in a private sale, according to Fanatics Collect, which says it brokered the deal.

The sale smashes the previous publicly known record for a Cristiano Ronaldo card, which was $312,000 for his 2002-03 Panini Mega Craques rookie card in a Gem-Mint PSA 10 grade via auction in 2021. This is also the second most expensive known soccer card sale of all time, behind the $1.5 million paid for Lionel Messi’s 2004 Panini Mega Cracks rookie card in a PSA 10 grade with the MBA Gold Diamond distinction (for exceptional eye-appeal in the grade) in a private sale also brokered by Fanatics Collect last year.

The announcement comes as Ronaldo celebrates winning the Saudi Pro League for the first time.

The $1.35 million Ronaldo card is his 2018 Panini Kaboom Green parallel, of which only one was printed. Panini’s Kaboom sets have been some of the most popular and valuable inserts of the ultra-modern era across multiple sports, due in part to their eye-catching comic-inspired art. The 50-player 2018 set, which was only available in multisport packs from a Panini Rewards program release, added the Green 1/1 parallel to the standard base versions launched five years earlier. The set is particularly sought-after among high-end collectors for that reason.

In February, The Athletic spoke to one such collector known as “Benjamin Be” on Instagram, who acquired 25 of the 50 Green 2018 Kabooms with the purchase of former NFL quarterback Josh Rosen’s card for $26,400.

“I think Kabooms will stand the test of time,” Be said at the time. “They are the most popular inserts from the Panini era. But I didn’t collect this set as an investment. I think it’s the coolest set and I just wanted to own it.”

Be told The Athletic on Thursday that he was not the buyer of the Ronaldo card.

Fanatics Collect did not reveal the identities of the buyer or the seller, but Instagram user “Cherubcards,” who previously posted about acquiring it in March 2024, told The Athletic they were the seller in the deal.

This sale is the latest sign that the soccer card marketing is heating up ahead of this summer’s World Cup. A 2015 Messi autographed card featuring a piece of an insole he wore during a match sold for $549,000 through Heritage Auctions last weekend.
